## 2. Requirement 1 — Official documentation and repository

**Documented facts:**
- Official website: `https://lightrag.github.io` — identified as "the official website" in the repository summary (call-45e5d64e). It was **not directly fetched**, so accessibility and currentness are unverified (step_1:claim_4 = unsupported).
- Official repository: `https://github.com/hkuds/lightrag` (also referenced as `HKUDS/LightRAG`; GitHub treats the owner case-insensitively). Public, MIT license, ~40.5k stars, ~5.7k forks, linked to arxiv.org/abs/2410.05779 (EMNLP2025) (step_1 observations; call-45e5d64e).
- Documentation lives in the repository's `docs/` folder; entries marked 🇨🇳 ship Chinese translations as `-zh.md`. Reference documentation includes `LightRAG-API-Server.md` and `ProgramingWithCore.md` (step_1 observations; call-9c4393a6; call-e475a33b).
- Config sample: `https://raw.githubusercontent.com/HKUDS/LightRAG/main/env.example` — fetched successfully (HTTP 200), documents all configurable environment variables (call-e5fcf6e7).

**Reasoned recommendation:** Use `https://github.com/hkuds/lightrag` as the source of truth and `https://lightrag.github.io` as the documentation entry point, but verify the docs site directly before relying on it for version-specific guidance.

---

## 3. Requirement 2 — Supported storage backends

LightRAG defines four storage roles (from `docs/ProgramingWithCore.md` via call-e475a33b and call-9c4393a6):

| Role | Purpose |
|---|---|
| KV_STORAGE | LLM response cache, text chunks, document information |
| VECTOR_STORAGE | Entity/relation/chunk embedding vectors |
| GRAPH_STORAGE | Entity–relation graph structure |
| DOC_STATUS_STORAGE | Document indexing/processing status |

### Backend matrix (evidence-backed)

| Category | Backend | Class / implementation | Notes | Sources |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Key-value | PostgreSQL | `PGKVStorage` | Production-recommended; single DB can serve all four roles | call-57f909ea; call-cb298109; call-e1579628 |
| Key-value | JSON / file | `JsonKVStorage` | Default; development/evaluation only | call-e475a33b; call-9c4393a6 |
| Key-value | MongoDB | `MongoKVStorage` | KV/graph/doc-status via MongoDB; vector only via Atlas | call-e475a33b; call-9c4393a6 |
| Key-value | Redis | (KV only) | Supported for KV; configure persistence/memory carefully | call-9c4393a6 |
| Vector | PostgreSQL + pgvector | `PGVectorStorage` | Requires `pgvector` extension | call-57f909ea; call-f7dbcdda |
| Vector | Local file | `NanoVectorDBStorage` | Default; dev/evaluation | call-e475a33b; call-9c4393a6 |
| Vector | MongoDB Atlas | `MongoVectorDBStorage` | Requires Atlas Search / Vector Search; local Docker Community Edition **cannot** serve this class | call-9c4393a6 |
| Vector | OpenSearch | (unified all four) | OpenSearch 3.x+ with k-NN plugin | call-9c4393a6 |
| Vector | Milvus / Qdrant / Weaviate | — | Mentioned in third-party comparisons for 10–100M vector scale | call-0b10ba97 |
| Graph | PostgreSQL + Apache AGE | `PGGraphStorage` | Requires Apache AGE extension | call-57f909ea; call-cb298109 |
| Graph | In-memory / file | `NetworkXStorage` | Default; dev/evaluation | call-e475a33b; call-9c4393a6 |
| Graph | Neo4j / Memgraph | `MemgraphStorage` etc. | Native graph engines; Memgraph integration documented by Memgraph | call-57f909ea; call-cb298109; call-70018081 (memgraph.com URL) |
| Document status | PostgreSQL | `PGDocStatusStorage` | Production-recommended | call-57f909ea; call-cb298109 |
| Document status | JSON / file | `JsonDocStatusStorage` | Default; dev/evaluation | call-e475a33b |
| Document status | MongoDB | `MongoDocStatusStorage` | — | call-e475a33b; call-57f909ea |

**OpenSearch** is notable as a unified single-backend option for all four roles (call-9c4393a6, official doc excerpt).

---

## 4. Requirement 3 — Differences between available storage options

**Documented facts:**
- Default stores (`NetworkX`, `NanoVectorDB`, JSON files) use in-memory databases and local file persistence; documentation is explicit that these are for development and debugging, **not production** (call-68d45e48 observations; call-cb298109; call-9c4393a6).
- PostgreSQL can serve all four roles with one instance: `PGKVStorage`, `PGVectorStorage`, `PGGraphStorage`, `PGDocStatusStorage`. Requires `pgvector` and Apache AGE extensions (call-57f909ea; call-23d05e40; call-cb298109).
- OpenSearch offers native k-NN vector search, full-text search, and horizontal scalability without cloud-only restrictions; requires OpenSearch 3.x+ with k-NN plugin (call-9c4393a6).
- MongoDB: local Community Edition (e.g., bundled Docker) supports KV/graph/doc-status but **not** `MongoVectorDBStorage`; vector requires MongoDB Atlas Search/Vector Search (call-9c4393a6).
- Redis is supported for KV only; persistence and memory usage must be configured carefully (call-9c4393a6).
- Specialized engines: Milvus/Qdrant for vector at scale; Neo4j/Memgraph for native graph traversal (call-8a6f1a23; call-9c4393a6).

**Reasoned comparison:**
- **Operational simplicity:** Single PostgreSQL instance < OpenSearch single backend < split PostgreSQL + specialized vector/graph engines.

These are not contradictory if read as "Redis can be production-grade for the KV role" versus "PostgreSQL is the recommended single-backend production choice." ## 6. Requirement 5 — Compatibility limitations and configuration considerations

**Documented facts:**
- Version constraints: OpenSearch 3.x+ with k-NN plugin (call-9c4393a6); LightRAG latest release noted as v1.5.5 (call-45e5d64e). No PostgreSQL/MongoDB/Neo4j version matrix found.

- Security: binding `HOST=0.0.0.0` without `LIGHTRAG_API_KEY`/`AUTH_ACCOUNTS` grants full network access; bind to `127.0.0.1` for local-only (call-e5fcf6e7).
- Known limitation: issue #2255 reports that updating LightRAG with PostgreSQL/Apache AGE is highly inefficient and causes long downtime during upgrade (call-57f909ea; call-cb298109; call-23d05e40).
- MongoDB limitation: local Docker MongoDB Community Edition cannot serve `MongoVectorDBStorage`; requires Atlas (call-9c4393a6).
- Backup/migration/upgrade: only the upgrade-downtime issue and the general observation that one Postgres instance means one backup/restore domain are documented (step_5:claim_4 = partially_supported).

**Reasoned considerations:**
- For production, set `LIGHTRAG_*_STORAGE` to the `PG*` classes and point all four at the same PostgreSQL instance to match the documented production pattern.
- Enable `pgvector` and Apache AGE; configure `POSTGRES_MAX_CONNECTIONS` and pooling based on concurrency needs (the `12` in issue #2255 is an example, not a requirement).
- Plan for upgrade downtime if using PostgreSQL + Apache AGE (issue #2255).
- Avoid `0.0.0.0` binding without authentication.

## 7. Requirement 6 — Recommended production storage architecture

**Source:** step_6 (completed), based on `https://github.com/hkuds/lightrag`, `https://lightrag.github.io`, `https://github.com/HKUDS/LightRAG/blob/main/docs/ProgramingWithCore.md` (call-8a6f1a23; call-45e5d64e).

### Recommended backends

| Storage category | Recommended backend (primary) | Scale-out alternative |
|---|---|---|
| Key-value | PostgreSQL (managed, e.g., Neon/AWS RDS) | MongoDB, OpenSearch |
| Vector | PostgreSQL + pgvector | Qdrant, Milvus |
| Graph | PostgreSQL (LightRAG graph over Apache AGE) | Neo4j, Memgraph |
| Document status | PostgreSQL | OpenSearch, MongoDB |

### Justification and trade-offs
- **PostgreSQL (all four roles):** Simplest deployment; one backup/restore and monitoring domain; ACID consistency for KV and doc-status; pgvector provides competent vector search without a separate system. Trade-off: vector throughput and graph traversal depth will not match purpose-built engines at very large scale; graph depends on LightRAG's implementation over Postgres rather than a native graph engine.
- **MongoDB:** Native KV and vector support with document-model flexibility. Trade-off: vector requires Atlas; not a clean single-backend answer for all roles.
- **OpenSearch:** Unified single backend for all four roles; horizontal scalability. Trade-off: heavier operational footprint than PostgreSQL; different consistency characteristics.
- **Qdrant/Milvus (vector):** Better recall/throughput at scale, richer indexing. Trade-off: extra cluster to operate, back up, and secure.
- **Neo4j/Memgraph (graph):** Native graph traversal. Trade-off: extra infrastructure, licensing (Neo4j), consistency boundaries with Postgres.

### Proposed deployment topology
```
AI Agent (LightRAG) ──► Managed PostgreSQL (primary)
                        ├─ KV storage (PGKVStorage)
                        ├─ Vector storage (PGVectorStorage + pgvector)
                        ├─ Graph storage (PGGraphStorage + Apache AGE)
                        └─ Document status (PGDocStatusStorage)
```
Scale-out variant: split vector to Qdrant/Milvus and graph to Neo4j/Memgraph while keeping KV and doc-status on PostgreSQL. LightRAG supports per-category backend selection, so this is a supported migration path (step_6 answer).

### Monitoring, backup, maintenance (partially evidenced)
- Single PostgreSQL instance simplifies backup/restore and monitoring into one domain (step_6 answer; details truncated in available excerpt).
- No detailed monitoring metrics, backup schedules, or maintenance procedures were captured in the evidence.

### Risk mitigation
- Use the per-category backend selection to migrate incrementally (scale-out variant) rather than fork-lift replacement.
- Test PostgreSQL upgrades on staging given the reported long downtime (issue #2255).
